### TUT-01 frozen implementation contract (2026-10-08)

Root and `tutorial_domain` reviewed real action/save boundaries. TUT-01 complete; TUT-02 implementation active. Names below are the agreed interface, not evidence that all runtime hooks exist. TUT-02 tests execute before TUT-03 is marked active. The lead will serialize Unity runs and checkpoints. Domain owner exclusively writes ShopTutorial.cs/SaveStore.cs and tutorial domain/save/format tests; root owns ShopTutorialSession.cs/ShopSession.cs/ShopStaffSession.cs, evidence and AGENTS. No UI files are assigned in this bounded foundation group.

**Domain API.** Pure C# `ShopTutorial`; `TutorialMode` Offered/Active/Completed/Skipped/LegacyUnguided; `TutorialActionOrigin` Player/Worker (all three staff roles share non-player classification; runtime preserves concrete origin at the hook). `TutorialLesson` None plus Orient/Collect/Prepare/Grow/Display/PriceAndOpen/Serve/Practice/CloseAndReview/NextPlan maps to ON01–10. `TutorialFacts` contains Moved, Looked, LabVisited, BloomCollected, FlowCollected, RecipePrepared, CreatureReady, CreatureDisplayed, PriceViewed, ShopOpened. Enum ranges and unknown bits are rejected.

`new ShopTutorial()` creates Offered; `LegacyUnguided()` creates the migration mode. Read-only properties Mode, Facts, FirstSaleAccommodationActive, PracticeAssisted; `CurrentLesson(ShopDayCycle)` derives the next unmet lesson. `Start()`, `Skip()`, `MarkPracticeAssisted()`, `Finish(ShopDayCycle)` return whether the state changed, not persistence success. Finish needs both manual loops, a qualifying acknowledged report, and Night after the practice sale's day. Repeated commands cannot award progress or rewards.

Observation API: `ObserveOrientation(bool moved,bool looked,bool inLab)`; `ObserveCollection(GameModel,CultureKind,ActionResult,TutorialActionOrigin)`; `ObservePrepared(GameModel,string speciesId,TutorialActionOrigin)`; `ObserveStarted(GameModel,ActionResult,TutorialActionOrigin)`; `ObserveReady(GameModel)`; `ObserveDisplayed(GameModel,ActionResult,TutorialActionOrigin)`; `ObservePriceViewed()`; `ObserveOpened(bool success)`; `ObserveSale(GameModel,ActionResult,TutorialActionOrigin,int day)`; `ObserveReportAcknowledged(int day)`. Methods return changed, accept only valid successful outcomes and cross-check the actual model/ID/location as applicable. Tutorial owns no currency, doses, creatures, claims or day clock. `Reconcile(GameModel)` clears unavailable unfinished candidates without erasing learned concepts or committed sale receipts; it never transfers items.

`CaptureSave()` returns a detached bounded snapshot. `TryRestore(TutorialSave,GameModel,int currentDay,out ShopTutorial)` validates schema, mode/flag dependencies, identity/species, live candidates, chronology and handoff consistency. DTO `TutorialSave`: version1, mode, facts, firstSaleAccommodationEnded, practiceAssisted, reportAcknowledged, handoffCompleted, reportDay, practiceBlockedSpecimenId and first/practice `TutorialChainSave` objects. Each chain has specimenId/speciesId, ready, manuallyDisplayed, saleDay. Empty chains use empty IDs/false/0. Sold chains are immutable receipts. Only two chains; no event history or Unity references.

When the first qualifying sale occurs, record any unrelated already-started incubator ID as practiceBlockedSpecimenId. That single exclusion is necessary so replaying a successful pre-sale start cannot masquerade as a new practice batch. It is not a third progression chain; the first chain is already a completed receipt. Clear the exclusion when a genuinely later valid manual start begins. A worker sale ends arrival grace but does not complete either manual proof. An invalidated unfinished candidate yields to a new manual batch; completed concepts survive.

**Save contract.** Envelope20, game6/report4 unchanged; SlotData.tutorial defaults Offered for an explicitly fresh slot. All reads of versions1–19 explicitly migrate to LegacyUnguided. Strict JSON shape checks require every tutorial field, correct primitive/object types and unique keys before JsonUtility can invent default values; then domain consistency validation runs. Current-format missing/invalid/future tutorial data preserves original bytes and blocks read/write. First migration write keeps exact .vN.bak. Root adds the minimum runtime property/restore/reset/capture plumbing during03 so existing staff snapshots carry tutorial data; this does not count as04 action/lifecycle completion or a player-visible tutorial. New Game replaces the state only after existing successful reset write. No second save file.

## FX — Living Shop effects and animation specification

Planning checkpoint: **2026-10-11**. Owner: root. **Current status: FX-PLAN, FX-00–05, FX-06R-00–07, FX-07, FX-08, FX-09, FX-10, FX-11, FX-12, FX-13, FX-14, FX-15, FX-16, FX-17 and FX-18 are technically delivered. FX-06R-08 and human review gates FX-06/24 remain open; the user explicitly authorized provisional continuation. FX-19–24 remain planned.** This specification follows the user's answers and takes priority for the next requested presentation assignment. It preserves the R08.4 game; R08.5, R09 and the deferred tutorial remainder are not completed by this plan.

### FX.1 — Approved direction, purpose and bounded scope

**User requirements:** improve all seven areas: lab machines, siphon/player interactions, creatures/tanks, customers/workers, comedy, rooms and UI. Highest priority, in order: **lab machines; siphon/player actions; creatures and tanks**. The user finds the whole lab and shop tanks weak and uninteresting. Use **cozy and bouncy motion with bigger comedy moments**, visible cartoon hands holding/operating the siphon and performing other interactions, and matching original locally produced sound effects through the existing audio system. Preserve the approved cozy aquatic shop, quirky science lab, their full separation and opaque door. The2026-10-12 refinement prioritizes hatching, dosing and growing creatures, requests all three particle styles and all living ambient details, and names the swirling siphon intake plus bubble-cloud incubator release as hero moments; see FX.10. No external reference game was supplied.

**Design response:** the lab should feel like a small living production workshop: visible fluid, valves, gauges and mechanisms communicate what is actually happening. The shop should feel like a miniature aquarium gallery: distinct fish movement, attractive water, small habitat motion and clearly presented stock. Motion gives anticipation, a readable action and a soft settling beat. Larger comic accents are occasional rewards; routine actions remain quick and comfortable over repeated shifts.

This is a presentation pass on the current game, not another static room redesign. Preserve approved silhouettes/materials and add movable visual parts only where needed. Cover all current supported station/display variants, four cultures and five existing species. Future R09 species receive an extensible animation convention; adding the remaining roster is not an FX task. No new recipes, feeding/death systems, production processes, customer archetypes, workers, prices, delays, payouts or inventory mechanics are introduced. No full player body or camera-mode change is required.

The deliverable is a playable, integrated pass, with source assets and evidence, not a concept reel. First produce one real growing-to-sale sample in the existing rooms, review its motion/sound in game, then expand the same implementation. A successful technical run and creative approval remain separate gates.

### FX.2 — Motion, effects and sound direction

- **Shop:** warm, gentle, buoyant movement; restrained water shimmer, soft bubbles, drifting plants and curious creatures. Busy displays must remain readable from the aisle. Keep prices, reservations, focus prompts and fish silhouettes clear.
- **Lab:** springy mechanisms and colorful fluid; purposeful pump strokes, valves, gentle vessel agitation and expressive gauges. Add contrast between idle, working, ready and blocked. Ambient activity must never imply an unavailable ingredient or uncommitted production step.
- **Hands/tool:** rounded proportions and simple readable fingers; a steady grip, small anticipation, a clear nozzle action and a short recovery. Keep the crosshair and station outlet visible. No default camera shake or added head bob.
- **Characters:** soft weight shifts and purposeful gestures. Match steps to actual travel; distinguish browsing, waiting, checkout and work. Cartoon exaggeration belongs primarily in reactions and comedy.
- **Timing defaults for the sample:** small hover/press accents80–180ms; routine gesture/effect200–600ms; exceptional hatch/discovery accent roughly1–1.5s, nonblocking and interruptible. These are tuning starting points, not extra simulation delays or measured player preferences.
- **Hierarchy:** command refusal/transaction/readiness feedback wins over celebration; important actions win over ambiance. Full buffers and blocked jobs get calm, persistent shape/text cues, not repeated warning flashes or constant error sounds.

| Surface / trigger | Intended visual and animation | Audio and important constraint |
|---|---|---|
| Bloom/Flow grower idle and refill |Small organisms drift; gentle bubbles and mechanism movement; liquid/availability presentation derives from actual capacity. Depletion visibly settles, refill gradually restores the real amount.|Low burble/pump texture. No decorative flow that suggests collectable stock in an empty grower.|
| Spark/Mist sources and conditioner |Distinct spark flutter versus curling mist; subtle coil/valve movement; conditioner shows loaded/working/ready/blocked states.|Soft fizz or airy puff, tied to the actual installed/unlocked facility; no invented machine or hazardous gameplay.|
| Manual collection |Continuous curved intake ribbon/droplets from focused reachable outlet into the nozzle; chamber fluid responds to committed collection; nozzle and fingers react softly.|Gentle suction with discrete collected-unit accents; stop on release, full/empty state, lost focus, pause or blocked collection.|
| Dosing / known-recipe preparation |Hand grip shifts, nozzle gives a measured pour/pulse into the correct station, staged colors mix visibly and settle.|Small pour/click accents. Never show accepted doses for a rejected command or replace a manual mixture cosmetically.|
| Incubator working |Gentle fluid circulation, moving ring/gauge/valve, readable progress; restrained light warmth as the real batch advances.|Quiet cycling texture, not a constant alarm. Animation cannot speed up incubation or charge for another batch.|
| Ready / first hatch |One soft mechanical reveal or canopy lift where bounds allow, fluid settles, bubble/sparkle accent, fish uncurls/wakes and settles into its ready pose.|Short hatch plop and discovery accent; repeats use a smaller ordinary-ready cue. No compulsory cutscene or replay on reload.|
| Research / upgrade |Brief scan/blueprint unfold/indicator response for the actual successful unlock or purchase; bench has restrained idle motion.|Paper/electronic chime; no false research progress, extra unlock or physical footprint expansion.|
| Collector / Doser automation |Module pump/light/outlet accent for real automatic operations; clear waiting/off/paused/blocked states, visually distinct from the player's siphon.|Sparse ticks/plips; no phantom player hands, fake material transfer or sound on every blocked retry.|
| Tank habitat |Stylized surface sheen, a few soft bubble lanes, mild water-light pattern and gentle plant motion; adapt to fixed/small/large tanks and legal positions.|Quiet water texture. Empty displays remain visibly empty; do not add saleable decorative fish.|
| Creature movement |Natural changes of speed/direction with fin/tail/body coordination, brief pauses, blinks and species-specific idle accents. Variation is deterministic and bounded.|Occasional restrained personality accents only when appropriate; do not fill the store with repeating squeaks.|

No gore, obscuring clouds or gameplay hazard.|
| Door and room transitions |Ease existing door movement, add a small mechanism/sensor response and localized light atmosphere; day/night lighting changes gently.|Short motor/slide and room-specific low ambiance. Preserve opaque separation, clearance, collision, reversal and pause behavior.|
| UI |Stable hover/press response, light panel settle, one progress/readiness/discovery accent and short delta toast after success.|Sparse UI ticks/confirms. Hit targets, keyboard focus, scrolling and Escape stay immediate and stable.|

### FX.3 — Hands, creatures and visual ownership

**First-person action set:** idle grip; movement-linked tool sway without camera motion; collect start/hold/end; dose start/end; successful interact/place; refused interact; tool upgrade settle; slap start/contact/recovery. Left hand supports and right hand grips the tool, with clear nozzle direction. Use local attachments appropriate to the existing camera/tool model. Hide/relax/cancel action poses when a modal, lost focus, arrangement, pause, quit or reload makes them inappropriate. Existing collection input and the remappable slap action remain unchanged. An E/menu action can remain immediate; the visual gesture follows the accepted action and never becomes a timed input lock.

Direct player transfer uses a brief vessel/place cue. Where no actual transport mechanic exists, do not invent a persistent held specimen or force a walk back to the destination. Animation represents existing accepted commands. A hand must not reach through a wall or interact beyond the established station reach. A missing hand, clip or attachment has a safe idle fallback and cannot break interaction.

**Current species assignments:** Pondlet is curious and springy with petal-fin flicks; Bubblebelly feels buoyant/heavier with a small body wobble; Ribbonfin uses a smooth slower ribbon wave; Lanternfin combines fin flutter with a warm restrained lantern pulse; Driftwing has light wing strokes and gliding pauses. These are recommended defaults to tune in the hero sample. Preserve silhouettes and container-specific scale. Do not give every fish identical synchronized loops, abrupt reversals, constant spins or human facial expressions by default.

Container placement owns the swim root; species animation owns fins/tail/body details. Displays, incubation vessels and rack containers have different movement envelopes. Sweep the entire animated mesh, including fins/tails, through turns, bobbing and maximum deformation at all supported container scales. Keep it inside the actual water/container bounds. Personality is visual only: no hunger, stress, new rarity or price effect.

For transfers, retain one visual owner for each specimen ID. Carry proxies are presentation only; the model's incumbent incubator/rack/tank ownership remains authoritative until its established durable transaction. Cancellation, failed writes, destination removal, worker dismissal, reload and reuse of pooled objects must release/hide stale proxies. A late animation callback cannot publish a second fish or payment.

### FX.8 — Validation matrix and review gates

For each newly affected surface, cover idle/working/ready/blocked/absent where supported; successful/rejected/repeated commands; pause/resume, focus loss, panel open/close, arrangement/relocation, worker interruption and save/reload/reset. Do not invent unsupported states to fill a checklist. Run isolated profiles only, preserving the normal slot and any existing player/editor/Blender sessions. Verify exact application identity rather than relying on old tooling receipts.

| Evidence | What it can establish |
|---|---|
| Source/asset audit |Owner, trigger, bounds/import/provenance intention; not rendered appeal or working input.|
| Automated domain/runtime assertions |State/resource conservation, duplicate/recovery safeguards, bounded lifecycle and ordinary action route under documented fixtures.|
| Actual Unity/Windows captures and motion clips |Visible materials, composition, timing, deformation, water layering and transitions at named resolution/build; not tactile feel or listening by themselves.|
| Native keyboard/mouse and audible playback |Held/released collection, clicks/focus/scroll, practical readability and heard mixes; record performed actions and device/setup.|
| Profiler/reproducible timings |Measured runtime cost and resource/allocation behavior on named hardware/settings; not a universal minimum PC specification.|
| Human playtest |Lab/tank appeal, satisfying actions, comfort, audio fatigue and repeated-shift enjoyment; record feedback and sample/build rather than assuming approval.|

**Review gates:** FX-06 evaluates the priority sample before multiplying content; FX-22 checks the complete supported presentation technically; FX-24 closes human creative/usability feedback. If feedback is absent, mark the affected human gate pending and continue only independent already-approved technical work, without calling creative acceptance complete. If a visual design fails the sample, revise that bounded slice before implementing the same failure across every asset.

### FX.9 — Completion and exact next assignment

FX is complete only when all planned tasks/required supported states have executed acceptance evidence, the final candidate runs the existing manual and automated loop, original local source/provenance is retained, and feedback/issues are explicitly resolved or recorded as user-accepted limitations. The lab/tanks must feel more alive in ordinary play, not only in a staged showcase. An acceptable final delivery includes playable build/scene, controls/settings, source/tag, before/after motion views, actual tests and measured limits, known issues and remaining wider-game gates.

**Next implementation assignment: FX-08 only on continuation.** FX-07 is technically complete; FX-06R-08 human controls/listening/creative acceptance and GPU decision remain deferred/open. Preserve current grower and earlier integrated players. No FX-08 work was included in this assignment.


### FX.10 — Stronger effects revision: confirmed feedback and complete work plan (2026-10-12)

**Status:** FX-06R-00–07, FX-07, FX-08, FX-09, FX-10, FX-11, FX-12, FX-13, FX-14, FX-15, FX-16, FX-17, FX-18, FX-19 and FX-20 are technically delivered; FX-06R-08 human review and GPU decision remain open. The user explicitly deferred hands-on feedback and authorized provisional continuation. FX-21 is next only on continuation; not started here. Sol supports bounded work; Astra owns advanced implementation/review. No human acceptance or GPU pass is inferred.

**Confirmed user requirements:** all action families need clearly visible, stronger effects. Event priority is **1. hatching; 2. dosing the incubator; 3. creatures growing**. Combine colorful liquid streams/droplets/bubbles, magical science glow/trails/sparks/rings, and messy cartoon puffs/steam/fizz/small bursts. Everyday actions should read clearly, with larger hatch/discovery celebrations. Include all requested living detail: moving liquid in tubes, bubbling cultures, incubator steam/glow, subtle fish bubble trails, moving water/plants and occasional harmless science mishaps. The two named hero moments are a swirling intake into the siphon and an incubator release/pop in a colorful bubble cloud. No external reference was supplied. Existing cartoon hands, original matching sounds, cozy aquatic shop and quirky lab remain the direction.

**Design decision:** give every action one recognizable primary effect, one supporting response and a short settling beat. Combine the three styles across the palette; do not put every particle shape/color on every action. Lab operations can be punchier than shop ambiance. Each culture keeps its established color and visual identity; use rounded bubbles, broad curved streams, soft puffs and a few clear sparkle/ring accents. Glow must read with the existing URP setup, without assuming global bloom, new post-processing or a VFX Graph package. First discovery has the strongest burst; repeat hatches remain satisfying at lower density. Keep real fish and machine silhouettes visible throughout. New values below are **proposed tuning**, not implemented behavior or measured acceptance.

This revision supersedes the earlier minimal particle-density and subtle-intensity targets in FX.2 and Docs/Design/FX01_CUE_ASSET_CONTRACT.md. Existing attachment, scale, authority and cancellation contracts stay in force. R-01 now implements the64/32 Standard and24/8 Low split and12/6 logical emitter ceilings using8/4 and4/2 action/ambient partitions. The source-inspection values below remain the historical before reference.

#### Priority cue specification

| Event / actual trigger | Proposed visible effect and timing | Acceptance and ownership |
|---|---|---|
| First hatch / committed ready transition and actual first discovery | Brief vessel compression/glow, then a directional release of roughly 36–48 bubbles/droplets plus a soft puff and a sparse expanding sparkle ring. Peak in the first 0.15–0.55s; settle within 1.2–1.6s. Coordinate the existing Pondlet wake/uncurl and original hatch sound. Fit a small visual pop-open aperture/shutter/vent only if needed; retain the fixed approved outer frame. | Must be obvious from the ordinary operator view at 720p/1080p with the real HUD. No full-screen flash, camera shake, forced cutscene, altered incubation delay or second fish. Trigger once after the real saved result; loading an already-ready batch never replays discovery. |
| Repeat hatch / later committed ready transition | Roughly18–28 bubbles with a smaller puff/ring and springy specimen wake;0.7–1.0s. Keep a visible release instead of the current two tiny motes. | Clearly celebratory while less intense than discovery; immediately interactable. Pause/reload/rebuild and repeated refresh cannot repeat the burst. |
| Accepted dose into incubator | Colored curved stream/spiral into the actual vessel,12–18 motes plus a bounded mixing ripple/bubble response. Fluid/indicator reacts to the real staged composition; routine beat 0.35–0.6s, brief settle. | Start only after the accepted saved command. The actual dosing panel must show a local stream/ripple accent on its existing measured-dose area when it covers the vessel. No invisible world-only proof or hand reaching through a modal. Reject/return/clear have different truthful cues and no fake success pour. |
| Incubating creature growth / actual loaded working batch | Visible size/pose maturation, swirling fluid, staged bubbling and a slowly warming pulse driven by real normalized batch progress. Increase energy gently toward actual readiness; avoid an early hatch burst. | Fit the existing vessel envelope across the whole pose. No growth in empty/locked/absent stations; pause/blocked state settles correctly. Already-ready reload restores a quiet ready state. This is visual growth during existing incubation, not a new fish-aging mechanic. |
| Cultures refilling / real capacity and refill progress | Organisms drift, fluid circulates visibly in the vessel/internal tube, short bubble lanes and occasional fizz tied to actual refilling. Full and depleted states are visibly different. | Decorative cooling motion must not imply collectable output when empty. Do not invent transfer between unconnected machines. No constant full/blocked bursts or retry sounds. |
| Held culture collection / valid reachable outlet and accepted collection | A readable spiraling intake travels from the true grower outlet to the moving siphon mouth; droplets follow the curve and chamber fluid/hand recoil respond to accepted units. Intensity tapers on release. | The requested swirl must read at normal distance, for both tool capacities. Stop at release/full/empty/lost target/wall/modal/focus/pause; no imaginary stock, stale trail or particles through walls. Actual collection cadence and input remain unchanged. |
| Occupied aquarium / real saved specimen and ordinary swim | Fish has a subtle motion-linked bubble trail; a few habitat bubble lanes, water ripples/light accents and moving plants. Arrival placement has a short local bubble/settle accent. | Water detail works from the aisle and up close. Bubble trails remain inside water and stop for absent specimens. Empty tanks can retain gentle habitat water, but no creature trail/ghost. No extra saleable fish, tank root movement or permanent obscuring glow. |

#### All later action families inherit this direction

Research/upgrades get a readable scan/blueprint glow, ring and a brief sparkle confirmation after real success. Automation/module operations get real fluid pulses and nozzle puffs; worker pickup/place gets a vessel/ripple response at the actual source/destination. Sales/purchases get a local till/coin burst with readable money/price text. Slaps and existing comedy get a punchier contact puff, restrained stars and bouncy recovery; harmless lab fizz/mishaps are bounded visual variants of existing incidents, with no new hazard or economy. Door mechanisms and day/night transitions get local easing/light/steam detail. UI gets brief local press/progress/discovery/delta accents. These actions belong to the corresponding existing FX-07–20 tasks after the revised hero gate; none are quietly omitted from the full effects pass.

#### Budget, lifecycle and comfort contract

Extend existing FxCueRuntime/FxEffectPool and ShopWorld/ShopAudio owners; do not install a duplicate system. Source inspection confirms the current pool has 96 fixed mesh slots,24 action-reserved slots, a32 Low cap, and the current first/repeat hatch uses4/2 motes. Current attributable topology is112 renderers / 120 transforms, with its112-renderer ceiling already used. Density and curve/fade variation should first reuse those slots and shared assets. Proposed R-01 rebalance: at most 64 action slots with at most 32 ambient slots on Standard; Low at most 24 action/8 ambient, preserving at least one accepted-action cue. These are proposed capacity policies, not changes already made. Keep the current 16 active cue and12/6 Standard/Low logical emitter ceilings until measured evidence supports a documented revision. Ambient work yields to accepted actions and readiness.

Admit original local particle shapes/masks/shared materials only as needed within existing ceilings (at most 3 new shared materials/24 attributable meshes/180 transforms). Do not silently increase renderer/pool limits. If a different renderer representation is needed, measure and document the bounded topology change in R-01 before spreading it. Reuse materials; do not create/destroy a GameObject, material, mesh or AudioSource for every droplet. Reset curve/trail/color/age/owner data on pool reuse. All temporary cues are cosmetic, bounded and nonpersistent.

Cancel transient effects on pause, focus loss, arrangement, moved/removed owner, disable, reset and save/load; reconstruct persistent current-state visuals without replaying one-shots. Failed save, refused dose, full destination, reserved stock or canceled job produces appropriate feedback, never success particles or a second sound. Repeated accepted inputs coalesce safe visual accents without delaying commands or accumulating a queue. Missing effect/audio must leave gameplay intact.

Reduced motion keeps readable local bubbles/ripples and static shape/text cues, reduces expansion/squash and removes large trails. Low detail reduces density/opacity before removing essential feedback. No default camera shake, strobing or full-screen tint. Keep crosshair, dose controls, prices, queue/crew cards and tutorial targets readable. Presentation sound follows the existing original local audio system and service priority; stronger visuals do not imply louder, duplicated or permanently looping sounds. Saved comfort controls remain FX-20; the hero uses explicitly labeled existing diagnostic controls until then.

The earlier tank GPU uncertainty stays open. Use old source2fa5efc/unchanged review player as the before reference. Record actual CPU/GPU frame-time percentiles, allocations, resource counts and transparent overdraw at the same ordinary/busy720p/1080p views. Investigate any greater-than10% increase; do not claim a pass from the120FPS cap or aggregate averages. Add per-window continuous focus/overlap evidence where timing requires it, and record GPU clock variation. Wallpaper Engine pause is already authorized specifically for bounded profiling with immediate restoration; it is not permission to stop other apps. Do not repeat the completed old comparison instead of measuring the new candidate.

## UX — Cozy in-world UI redesign specification (2026-10-19)

Requested by the user on 2026-10-19 after reviewing every screen: *"very cluttered, unclear, badly designed and overall uncomfortable."* This section is the authoritative scope for the redesign. The milestone entry in section 9 points here. Nothing below is implemented yet; mockups are design input, not proof of native rendering.

### UX.1 — User decisions (2026-10-19)

| Question | User's answer |
|---|---|
| Station interaction | **In-world first.** A small card beside the machine; physical siphon actions for dosing and pricing. Full-screen views only for planning (crew, research, layout, automation, journal, report, settings). |
| HUD density | **Minimal and contextual.** Money, day/clock and one next-step line. Everything else appears when relevant and fades. |
| Screens in scope | **All of them:** HUD, lab panels, shop panels and meta screens. |
| Foundation | **Rebuild on Unity UI Toolkit** and rewrite the UI tests that click fixed coordinates. Game rules and saves stay untouched. |
| Look | **Cozy diegetic:** paper price tags, an order clipboard, enamel lab labels and gauges, chunky rounded shapes matching the warm shop and quirky lab. |
| Copy tone | **Short and a bit silly.** Verb-first, 1–4 words per button, a small joke where it costs nothing. Rule explanations live in Help. |
| Numbers | **Visual first, numbers on hover.** Faces, pips and bars; exact values on hover or while holding Alt. |
| Game feel | **Punchy but quick.** Snappy pop-in, coin fly-up, sale ka-ching, celebratory day report; nothing delays input; Reduced motion respected. |
| Controller | **Keyboard/mouse only, controller-ready.** Every screen gets a defined focus order so gamepad can be added cheaply later. |
| Process | **Spec and mockups first.** The user approves mockups before any Unity code changes. |

These answers supersede two older constraints: the `.agents/skills/unity-game-ui-ux` line "No ... UI Toolkit migration is implied", and the HUD comment that panel anchors are "deliberately retained for established input scenarios". Coordinate-based UI tests are rewritten, not preserved.

### UX.2 — Audit of the current UI (evidence for the redesign)

Reviewed `Runtime/ShopHud.cs` and its panel partials plus actual captures under `Docs/Evidence/fx-20/`, `fx-18/`, `fx-17/`, `fx-16/` and `fx-11/` (720p).

1. **One centred form for everything.** All 21 `ShopPanel` values draw into one fixed 580×518 card at screen centre with a scroll view. It hides the station being used, and important actions fall below the fold (Pause: *Save and resume* appears only after scrolling past slap settings).
2. **Copy written for the test harness.** Panels explain safety guarantees instead of the next action ("Unsupported mixtures never consume resources", "Sales minus staff wages: 12 credits / other investments excluded", an empty "RESEARCH / SAVED INSTALLATIONS" header). The " / " separator is used everywhere ("Pip / cashier", "Close / ESC", "Dismiss Pip / no wage refund").
3. **No hierarchy.** Nearly every button is the same mint pill; primary, secondary and destructive actions look alike. Heading, body and fine-print sizes are too close together.
4. **HUD crowding and duplication.** Up to ten persistent cards: day, "NO RUSH / Untimed preparation", next step, credits, rep/appeal, "Ready to create", shop & crew, discovery, siphon, permanent controls bar. Siphon fill also appears on the held tool.
5. **Physical actions buried in menus.** Dosing is +Bloom/−Bloom buttons; pricing is −5/−1/+1/+5 plus four lines of text reactions.
6. **World signs compete with the HUD.** Floating labels such as "2/2 / READY / COLL" and "MIST RESEARCH / E" clip and add noise.
7. **Technical lock-in.** IMGUI with hand-placed rectangles on a letterboxed 1280×720 canvas; tests click fixed coordinates, freezing the layout.

### UX.3 — Design principles (apply to every screen)

1. **Keep the world visible.** Using a station never covers that station. Station cards sit beside it; planning views dim the world rather than replace it.
2. **One job per surface.** Each card answers one question ("What do I make?", "What price?", "Who's waiting?"). If it needs a scroll bar at 1280×720, split it.
3. **Three button levels.** One *primary* action per card (filled teal), *secondary* actions (outlined), *destructive* actions (coral, behind a confirm step or hold). Disabled buttons say why on hover.
4. **Verb-first labels, no " / ".** 1–4 words: "Start", "Serve", "Open shop", "Hire Pip". Key hints are separate key-cap glyphs, not text.
5. **Show state, not guarantees.** Status words, pips, rings and faces. Safety rules and edge-case explanations move to Help (F1) and tooltips.
6. **Visual first, numbers on demand.** Every bar, pip or face exposes its exact value on hover or while Alt is held.
7. **Feedback within 100 ms, never blocking.** Presentation follows the authoritative result (existing FX ownership rule) and never delays the next command.
8. **Comfort.** Reduced motion and Effects detail settings scale or remove UI motion. Nothing important is shown by colour alone.

### UX.4 — HUD

**Always visible (only these):**
- **Top-left day chip:** sun/moon icon, "Day 3", and the trading clock inside the same chip ("4:12 left"). At night it reads "Night 3 · no rush" with no timer card.
- **Top-right money:** coin icon and credits. Sale income flies from the counter into it and ticks up.
- **Bottom-centre next step:** one line ("Mix a Bloom and a Flow in the lab"). It fades after 10 s without change and returns when the objective changes or F1 is pressed. During the tutorial it stays.

**Contextual (appears, then fades):**
- **Queue strip** under the day chip while customers wait: one face per customer with a patience ring; it turns coral when patience is low.
- **Ready pings:** "Pondlet ready" toast plus an edge-of-screen arrow when the source is off-screen (incubator, vat, worker blocked).
- **Rep and appeal:** small "+2 ★" floater at the moment it changes; full values live in the day report and journal.
- **Discovery stamp:** a large one-time card with the new silhouette, then it moves into the journal.
- **Comedy captions:** speech bubbles anchored to the speaking character, not a screen-fixed bar.

**Removed:** the "NO RUSH" card, "Ready to create" card (replaced by ready pings), persistent "Shop & crew" card (replaced by the queue strip and worker status in the crew view), HUD siphon card (the tool readout stays), and the permanent controls bar (key hints sit on the interaction prompt; F1 shows the full control sheet).

**Interaction prompt:** a small tag beside the crosshair: key-cap glyph, station name, one live status word. Examples: `[E] Incubator · 7s`, `[Hold LMB] Bloom grower · full`, `[F] Slap · ready`.

### UX.5 — Station cards (in-world)

Common pattern: a card up to 380 px wide (1080p reference) anchored beside the station's screen position, flipped to the other side when near an edge and clamped on-screen. Opening a card frees the cursor; Escape, E or stepping away closes it. Simulation keeps running, as today. Each card has a title strip in the station's material (enamel label for lab, paper tag or clipboard for shop), a status line, the content, and one primary action.

- **Incubator:** recipe tiles for known species (silhouette, culture pips, time). Clicking a tile doses from the siphon in one step; manual doses use culture chips with − / + and the mouse wheel. A shortage shows the missing culture in coral with "Grab Flow at the grower". Primary: **Start · 10s**. Secondary: *Return doses*. While growing, the card shows a progress ring and the fish silhouette filling in.
- **Display tank (price tag):** a paper tag with the price large; − and + buttons (Shift for ±5, wheel works); a row of four customer faces (happy = bargain/fair, neutral = pricey but buys, frown = too expensive, wallet-X = over budget) and "3 of 4 will buy". Hover a face for the exact reaction and limit. Small link: *Use standard (10)*. An empty tank shows ready stock to place as tiles.
- **Counter (order clipboard):** waiting customers as rows (face, species, agreed price, patience ring). Primary: **Serve**. Day controls as a large switch: at night **Open shop · 8:00** with warnings above it ("1 display empty"); by day *Close early* with a confirm step. Links to Crew, Arrange and last report.
- **Specimen rack, conditioning vat, research bench, collector/doser:** same pattern. One status line, contents as tiles, one primary action ("Store", "Start vat · 20s", "Research Spark · 48", "Turn on").

### UX.6 — Planning views (full screen, world dimmed)

Notebook/clipboard metaphor, tabs along the top, no scrolling at 1280×720 for the default tab. Escape always backs out one level.

- **Crew:** three portrait cards (Pip cashier, Nori stocker, Moss lab technician). Each card: what they do in one line, wage per duty period, an **On duty** toggle, current status chip ("Serving", "Idle: no stock"). Pause and Dismiss live in a "…" menu; Dismiss needs a confirm.
- **Automation:** one row per known species: target stepper (1–9), destination picker, on/off, status chip with the blocked reason in plain words.
- **Arrange:** catalogue grid (thumbnail, price, appeal, slots) with tabs Furniture / Decor / Owned / Lab. "Place" enters the existing placement mode; placement hints move to a bottom key bar shown only during placement.
- **Research:** the four cultures as cards on a short path (Bloom, Flow, Spark, Mist): requirements as discovery stamps, cost, one **Research** button. Siphon MK II sits on the same screen as equipment.
- **Journal:** tabs Creatures / Customers / Shop. Creatures is a grid of silhouettes; discovered ones show recipe pips, family and standard price; undiscovered ones show the clue. Customers shows the four portraits with budget, patience and favourites as icons. Shop shows reputation tier and appeal with what the next tier gives.
- **Day report:** a receipt slip. Headline income counts up; three stats (sold, visitors, missed); a missed-sales line only lists non-zero reasons; one tip for tonight; primary **Next night**. Wages and other details on hover.
- **Pause:** left column Resume / Settings / Help / Save & quit. Settings tabs: Controls (sensitivity, slap key), Sound (master, ambience, humor), Comfort (reduced motion, effects detail, reduced gags). Reload save and New game sit under a "Save file" section with confirm steps. Dev-only buttons (presentation sample, comedy preview) appear only in development builds.
- **Welcome and tutorial help:** ported into the same visual language. The TUT lesson logic and saved state are unchanged; remaining TUT-11–14 stays deferred.

### UX.7 — Copy rules and example rewrites

Rules: verb-first; buttons 1–4 words; status words, not sentences; no " / " separators; one joke at most per card and never on a warning; explanations go to Help or tooltips; numbers always carry their unit icon.

| Current | New |
|---|---|
| Begin incubation / 10 sec | Start · 10s |
| Return all doses safely | Return doses |
| Doses reserve room in your siphon until incubation begins. Unsupported mixtures never consume resources. | (Help tooltip) |
| Close for the night... | Close early |
| Open for day 1 | Open shop |
| Continue preparation / ESC | Next night |
| Dismiss Pip / no wage refund | Dismiss Pip… (confirm: "Pip packs up. Today's wage stays paid.") |
| Pause work / no refund | Pause |
| Use standard price / 10 credits | Use standard (10) |
| Too expensive, won't buy | Nope, too pricey |
| SHOP CREDITS | (coin icon only) |
| Untimed preparation | no rush |
| Placement cancelled. Your room layout and credits are unchanged. | Placement cancelled |
| Creature stored. The incubator is free for the next recipe. | Stored on rack 1 |

### UX.8 — Visual language

- **Palette:** keep `ShopUiTheme` (Paper, Ink, Teal, Coral, Honey, Muted) and the culture colours (Bloom coral-orange, Flow blue, Spark gold, Mist lilac). Add a darker paper for nested surfaces and a kraft tan for tags. Contrast for text at least 4.5:1.
- **Materials:** shop surfaces are paper tags with a string hole, clipboards and receipt slips; lab surfaces are enamel labels with rivets, glass gauges and dials. Rounded chunky corners, a soft drop shadow, no thin hairlines.
- **Type:** a rounded display face for headings and numbers and a sturdy humanist sans for body, both open-licensed (proposal: Baloo 2 and Nunito, SIL OFL) with provenance recorded under R11.3. At the 1920×1080 reference: headings 32–40 px, body 20 px, small 16 px, nothing below 14 px. UI scale setting 90–130% under Comfort.
- **Icons:** one consistent set (culture drops, coin, star, sun/moon, faces, key caps) drawn as simple filled shapes; no emoji.

### UX.9 — Game feel

- Card open: 120 ms scale 0.94→1 with slight overshoot plus a soft paper or enamel click; close in 80 ms.
- Button press: 60 ms squash and a tick sound; disabled press: 2 px shake and a dull thunk with the reason tooltip.
- Price change: the tag wiggles and faces swap with a small bounce.
- Sale: ka-ching, coins fly from the counter into the money chip (≈450 ms), money ticks up.
- Discovery: stamp-down animation with the existing discovery sound.
- Day report: tallies count up over 600 ms (any input skips to the end), then the tip slides in.
- Reduced motion: no scale/shake/fly; fades only. Effects detail Low: no particles on UI.
- All UI feedback reuses the existing FX ownership rule: it plays only after the authoritative result and never delays the next command.

### UX.10 — Technical plan

- **Framework:** UI Toolkit runtime (`UIDocument`, UXML, USS) with one `PanelSettings` at 1920×1080 reference, scale-with-screen, match 0.5. Layout uses flex; no absolute pixel layout except world-anchored cards.
- **Presenters:** each screen gets a small presenter that reads `ShopSession`/`GameModel` state and calls the existing command methods (`SetSpeciesPrice`, `OpenForDay`, serve, dose, hire, etc.). UI never mutates money, stock or saves directly; all current command validation stays authoritative.
- **World anchoring:** cards follow `Camera.WorldToScreenPoint` of the station's interaction anchor, clamped and side-flipped; they never cover the anchor itself.
- **Input:** Input System UI module; cursor freed while a card or planning view is open; every screen has a defined focus order and a Back action, so gamepad support can be added later.
- **Strings:** all player-facing text in one string table (keys per screen) so wording can change without code edits; no translation is claimed.
- **Migration:** the IMGUI path stays behind a development toggle until each replacement reaches parity, then is deleted in UX-09. The FX-18 IMGUI accents are re-implemented as USS transitions.
- **Tests:** rule, save, ledger and staff tests are untouched. UI tests switch from coordinate clicks to named-element queries (`Q<Button>("serve")`) and real click events. Existing validation scenarios keep their gameplay assertions.

### UX.11 — Ordering relative to other open work

FX-21–23 (integrated interruption, native visual/input/performance validation and tester candidate) validate the UI that this milestone replaces. **Claude's scheduling decision (2026-10-19), open to user override:** run UX-02 through UX-09 before FX-21–23, so that integrated QA validates the final UI once. FX-24, R08.5, TUT-11–14 and all open human gates keep their status.

Accept: an empty themed card opens and closes from a station at 720p/1080p/2560×1080 with real input.

Accept: full manual loop (collect → dose → start → place → price → open → serve → close) playable with new UI; no scroll at 1280×720; one primary button per card.

- [x] UX-09 (technically complete 2026-10-21; human playtest deferred; see UX.20) Delete the IMGUI path, finish UI test migration, full EditMode plus Windows player routes at 1280×720, 1920×1080 and 2560×1080, and a human playtest of the whole loop.

Milestone gate: a new player can run a full night/day loop without reading a paragraph; every station is used without covering it; the HUD shows at most three persistent elements; all gameplay, save and staff tests still pass; the user reports the UI as clear and comfortable.

## AD — Pocket Aquarium Diorama: art, effects and gameplay redesign (2026-10-19)

Proposed by Claude on 2026-10-19 after an audit of current captures (concept canvas "Evolution Shop Redesign Proposal", eight boards). The user replied: *"in the final game i want a lot more than a few (15) collectables it need to take time to get them all so its ok, other than that yes to the rest."* This section is the authoritative scope for the redesign. Concept sketches are direction, not final art or proof of native rendering.

### AD.1 — User decisions (2026-10-19)

| Question | Decision |
|---|---|
| Overall look | **Yes: Pocket Aquarium Diorama.** Keep the cozy aquatic shop and quirky lab, the room split and opaque door; push to chunky toy-like shapes, warm practical light and glowing creatures. |
| Toon shading, outlines and bloom | **Yes.** Two-step soft toon lighting with rim light; thin dark outline on creatures and characters only; URP bloom plus one colour-grading Volume per room. This supersedes the R06.5 "first pass" materials and the FX.10 rule that glow must read "without assuming global bloom". |
| Colour variants | **Yes, and the collection must be large and take time to complete.** See AD.3. |
| Wish bubbles, tomorrow's forecast and the other gameplay changes | **Yes**, prototyped with placeholder art and playtested before they replace current behaviour. |
| Process | Prove the look on one slice (display corner + incubator) in game before rolling it out. |

### AD.2 — Audit findings (current build captures)

1. Expanded rooms are empty tile boxes (lab tier 3 especially).
2. Day and night look the same: no window, flat light; the rhythm is only visible on the HUD clock.
3. Customers are peg figures (tube limbs, no hands, tiny faces); hats are the only differentiator.
4. Creatures are small and can be low contrast (teal Driftwing in teal water inside a large incubator ring).
5. Crew and customers share one body and read the same at a glance.
6. The siphon's glass jar fills the lower right of the view; world signs are too small to read.

### AD.3 — Collection scope change (user decision, replaces section 5 "Discoveries")

The user wants far more than 15 collectables and a long completion. Claude's tuning default, open to revision after playtests:

- **24 species in 4 families of 6** (Brookkin, Sparkline, Airfin and a fourth Mist-led family), including the existing five. Each family shares one Blender rig; species differ by mesh, signature feature and idle habit.
- **4 colour variants per species = 96 journal entries.** Classic, Sunny (+Bloom), Deep (+Flow) and Shimmer (needs the conditioning vat or a later process). Variants are deterministic and learnable from recipes and journal clues; no required entry depends on a random roll (section 6.5 still applies). Variants are material/texture swaps, not new meshes.
- **Main ending stays the Grand Exhibition.** Unlock moves from "9 of 12 species" to **18 of 24 species** across all four families, including the signature species. Completing all 96 entries is an optional long-term goal, not a prerequisite.
- **Pacing goal:** collect-all should take well beyond reaching the ending. No campaign-hour promise; measure in R10 playtests. Higher variants and late families should be gated by research, facilities and processes, so collecting stays directed rather than grindy.
- **Market role:** Collectors pay more for entries they are missing; wishes (AD.6) can ask for a variant.

### AD.4 — Visual direction

- **Pillars:** chunky and squishy shapes; light tells the time; creatures are the jewels (only cultures and creatures get full saturation and glow); everything reacts (squash/stretch, fish look at the player, machines wobble on completion).
- **Lighting keys:** morning open, midday busy, closing amber lamps, night tank glow. The shop gets a street window; the lab keeps its cool mint grade.
- **Creatures:** about twice today's on-screen size; eyes a third of the head with highlights; one signature trick and one idle habit per species; family water tints so no species blends in (Driftwing lilac on warm sand water). Face shape keys: blink, happy, surprised, puffed.
- **Characters:** about 2.5 heads tall; mitten hands with a thumb; body shape per type (Casual round, Bargain tall/thin, Collector pear, Big spender wide coat). Crew always wear shop teal, customers never do. One humanoid rig; body types as shape keys; props on sockets; four reactions per type.
- **Rooms:** each tier adds a set piece (shop: window bench and hanging bowls, then a feature tank; lab: overhead pipe gallery, then a glass dome for Spark/Mist). Glowing glass pipes carry each culture's colour to the incubator. Fewer, bigger signs painted onto objects. Station positions, footprints, colliders, aisles and save IDs are unchanged; new art is decorative children.
- **Siphon:** slimmer, side-mounted chamber that shows carried culture colours; roughly a third less screen area.

### AD.5 — Effects language

- Six hand-drawn flipbook shapes on the built-in particle system: bubble, swirl, sparkle, puff, ripple, coin. No new package.
- Hatch hero moment (about 1.4 s, never blocks input): wind-up, 0.08 s presentation-only freeze beat (game clock keeps running), pop with bubble cloud, pose with NEW stamp, settle. Repeat hatches use wind-up, pop and settle.
- Sale: scoop into bag, bag ties, coins arc to the money chip, customer hop. Slap: impact star, spinning hat, brief cartoon birds. Refusal or blocked: small grey puff and shake only.
- Water: moving caustics on tank floors and walls, wobbling surface, fish bubble trails.
- Kept: the existing FX pool, cue ownership and cancellation rules, Reduced motion and Low detail (no freeze beat, flash or shake in Reduced motion).

### AD.6 — Gameplay changes (prototype first, then playtest)

- **Wish bubbles:** customers arrive with an icon wish (species, colour/variant, or a trait such as "glows"). Exact match gives a tip and a star point; close match leads to haggling. Uses existing archetypes, reservations and checkout; a wish is a preference, not a quest.
- **Tomorrow's forecast:** the night receipt previews tomorrow's visitors so the untimed night has a goal.
- **Hands-on checkout:** a one-second scoop-and-bag with the siphon replaces the Serve button; Pip still serves automatically when hired.
- **Shop stars:** a 1–5 star storefront sign replaces "Rep 0/100"; each star unlocks something visible (customer type, bigger budgets, the Exhibition at 5). Underlying reputation rules stay.
- **Tank themes:** decor sets a tank theme; matching species sell for more and attract certain customers.
- **Day length:** test 5–6 minute days with one rush event; decide from measured playtests.
- Kept: manual and automated paths, no fail states, Grand Exhibition ending.

### AD.7 — Order, tasks and gates

UX-02–UX-09 (approved UI redesign) run first. AD-A can start once UX-02 (UI Toolkit foundation) is in.

- [ ] AD-A Art slice: display corner + incubator at final quality: toon shading, outlines, bloom, room Volumes, shop window lighting keys, redesigned Pondlet and Casual visitor, full hatch moment, measured cost on the user's PC. **Gate: user reviews it in game before AD-B.** *Technically complete 2026-10-22, revision `ada-slice-1` (AD.8); the user approved it in game on 2026-10-22.*
- [ ] AD-B Creatures: family rigs, the five existing species redone, face shape keys, signature tricks, water tints, variant material atlas. *Technically complete 2026-10-22, revision `adb-creatures-2` (AD.9); the user approved them in game on 2026-10-22.*
- [ ] AD-C Characters: one humanoid rig, four customer bodies, three crew, hands, four reactions each. *Technically complete 2026-10-22, revision `adc-characters-1` (AD.10); the user approved them in game on 2026-10-22.*
- [ ] AD-D Rooms and effects: tier set pieces, lab pipe network, slim siphon, flipbook effects and sounds everywhere. *Technically complete 2026-10-22, revision `add-rooms-1` (AD.11); the user's look at them in game comes before AD-E.*
- [ ] AD-E Gameplay prototype: wishes, forecast, hands-on checkout, stars, tank themes, day length test. **Gate: user playtest.** *Technically complete 2026-10-23, revision `ade-proto-1` (AD.12); the user's playtest is its gate.*
- [ ] AD-F Content expansion: remaining species to 24 across four families and all 96 variant entries, folded into R09.3 and R09 progression gating. *Superseded 2026-10-23 by GR-12.*

Rules: original art only (Blender, local; no paid generation or bought assets without authorization); gameplay code stays authoritative; every phase ends in a playable build with real 1280×720 and 1920×1080 captures; performance is measured before effects spread; comfort settings scale every new moment.

### UX.14 — UX-03 HUD implementation record (2026-10-20, validated)

  - The interaction tag beside the crosshair (key caps, name, one status word) plus the slap tag.
  - The comedy bubble near the beat's source (recorded by `BeginComedyPresentation`), with a fallback spot when the source is off-screen.
  - The tutorial marker beside its target.

### UX.17 — UX-06 planning notebook implementation record (2026-10-21, validated)

**Decisions (Claude, within UX.6, UX.7 and UX.10):**

- **One notebook for five panels.** `PlanningViewPresenter` draws the dim, the sheet, the tabs (each with a where-to-go label when it can't be opened), the title, *Back*, the footer and the placement key bar. It registers `CrewView` (the Staff, Stocker and Technician panels), `StockerTargetsView`, `TechnicianQueueView`, `AutomationView`, `ArrangeView` and `ResearchView` (a new `ShopPanel.Research`, notebook only). Views read snapshots the session fills (`FillCrewView`, `FillStockerTargets`, `FillTechnicianQueue`, `FillAutomationView`, `FillArrangeView`, `FillResearchView` in `ShopToolkitPlanning.cs`) and call the existing commands through thin wrappers (`PlanHire`, `PlanSchedule`, `PlanPay`, `PlanPause`, `PlanDismiss`, `PlanRetry`, `PlanTile`, `PlanMoveOwned`, `PlanResearchSpark`, `PlanBuySiphon`). Pure rules (`PlanningRules`) carry the EditMode tests.
- **Guards widened, never bypassed:** the crew, automation and research commands also accept the notebook's own panel while it draws it, at the same station. Tabs open only what the player could open from where they stand (`PlanningTabAvailable`).
- **Esc** (`PlanningBack`, asked first by `BackFromPanel`): a crew page to the crew, a tab to the station card it was opened from while the player still stands there, otherwise back to play. Placement's Esc cancels back to Arrange.
- **Automation as one chosen recipe:** UX.6 drew a row per species with its own stepper, destination and switch, but the lab helper keeps one target recipe at a time, so the notebook lists the known recipes to *Choose* and sets the chosen one on the right. *Prepare one batch* is the one primary, its reason said once above it.
- **Research:** reached from the bench card's new *Research path* link; Mist says it is researched at the vat; Siphon MK II is equipment on the same page.
- **Placement:** the notebook steps aside and its key bar replaces the classic placement overlay while the preview is on.
- **The world dimmed** at alpha 0.76 (half brightness, as the mockup); the HUD keeps its day and money chips over it and hides its toasts, queue and stamp.
- **Footer:** the page's own line unless a notice raised on this page is current; save errors always; never the generic *Done.*

### UX.19 — UX-08 feel pass implementation record (2026-10-21, validated)

**Decisions (Claude, within UX.9 and UX.10):**

- **Pure motion rules** (`UiMotion`): each animation's duration and pose at an age, standard and reduced, plus the count-up and the coin arc; EditMode tests pin the numbers (card open 120 ms from 0.94 to about 1.009; close 80 ms to 0.96; press 60 ms at 1.04 × 0.92; disabled shake 2 px for 200 ms; price wiggle 6° and 8% for 280 ms; face hop 14% for 220 ms; stamp from 160% and -9° to its stylesheet's -2° in 260 ms; receipt tally 600 ms; coins about 450 ms; tip slide 18 px).
- **Reduced motion** keeps timing but replaces scale, shake, slide, tilt and flight with fades; numbers still count and every sound plays. **Low effects detail** only drops the coins (the UI's one particle effect).
- **One animator** (`UiAnimator`) applies inline opacity, scale, translate and rotate, one animation per element, and clears them when done so stylesheet values come back exactly; it runs on a feel clock advanced once per frame (capped at 0.25 s) before the presenters.
- **Closing never blocks:** a card is closed at once and every element in it ignores the pointer while it fades; E on another station mid-fade opens that card on the spot.
- **Sounds** (`ShopUiSounds`): five generated clips (paper, enamel, tick, thunk, ka-ching; 22050 Hz, deterministic, peaks 0.11 to 0.30) on one voice of the UI's own under the UI root, so the shop's five game voices (FX-19) are untouched. The stamp uses the lab's existing first-hatch sound.
- **Disabled presses** are picked by the feel itself (UI Toolkit may not deliver them); enabled presses come from a trickle-down handler on the root. The card's main button reuses its reason line; other buttons carry their reason as `tooltip`, which the feel draws as a tip.
- **Coins** start at the counter card's Serve button, else the counter on screen, and fly to the money chip's coin; a gain is a sale when today's ledger has a new sale since the last money cue (`ShopTradeLedger.CurrentSales`, read-only).
- **The receipt counts once per day**; **full-screen views only fade** (moving would change the UX-06 and UX-07 layout checks); **the classic dose strip** is not copied into the card, since the card never covers the incubator (FX-03's reason for the strip).
- **Strings:** 709 → 711 (the price steps' reasons).

**New files (EvolutionShop/Assets/EvolutionShop/):** `Runtime/UI/UiMotion.cs`, `UiAnimator.cs`, `UiFeel.cs`, `ShopUiSounds.cs`; `Runtime/ToolkitFeelSmoke.cs` (`-evolutionToolkitFeelSmoke`); `Tests/RuntimeEditMode/UiFeelTests.cs` (15 tests). Edited: `UI/ShopUiRoot.cs`, `UI/ShopUiPresenter.cs`, `UI/StationCardPresenter.cs`, `UI/StationCardViews.cs`, `UI/HudPresenter.cs`, `UI/ShopHudModel.cs`, `UI/ScreenReportView.cs`, `UI/ScreenPresenter.cs`, `UI/PlanningViewPresenter.cs`, `ShopToolkitHud.cs`, `ShopToolkitUi.cs`, `Core/ShopTradeLedger.cs` (two read-only counts), `ShopTokens.uss`, `CardStyles.uss`, `HudStyles.uss`, `strings.en.json`, `MilestoneSmoke.cs`, `ToolkitHudSmoke.cs`, `ToolkitScreensSmoke.cs`, `ToolkitUiSmoke.cs`.

### UX.20 — UX-09 IMGUI removal and full validation record (2026-10-21, validated)

**Decisions (Claude, within UX.10 and UX.12):**

- **One UI in every build:** `ShopUiRoot` is created at start-up in release and development builds and is on once it loads (`Active` is `Ready`). There is no preview switch on the root or the session, and F9 toggles nothing.

- **Kept, with an owner of their own:** the saved money change the HUD floats (`ShopUiFeedback.cs`, renamed from `ShopNativeUiFx.cs`); the next-step words and the last report (`ShopHud.cs`); the code-drawn icons (`ShopUiTheme`, now palette and icons only, made and disposed by `ShopUiRoot.Icons`).

### AD.8 — AD-A implementation record (2026-10-21 to 2026-10-22, Claude)

The user set FX-21 aside on 2026-10-21 and asked for the AD tasks; AD-A is the first.

**Decisions (Claude, within AD.1–AD.7):**

- **A development preview until the user's gate.** The look is on by default in development builds when played normally, off in every validation route unless asked for (`-evolutionDiorama`, or the slice route `-evolutionDioramaSliceSmoke`; `-evolutionDioramaOff` refuses it), and never in release builds. **F10** switches it in a played development build. Switching it off restores every material, mesh, light, shadow setting, ambient and Pondlet it changed; it changes no rule, save or station.
- **Scope of the slice:** the display corner (DISPLAY 01, DISPLAY 02 beside it, and the wall behind them) and the lab incubator take the new materials; every Pondlet becomes the kit Pondlet; Casual visitors become the kit visitor; the lighting keys, room grades and bloom are global. Other stations, rooms, species and customer types keep their art until AD-B to AD-D.
- **Rendering:** four original HLSL shaders in `Resources/` (so they are in the build): `EvolutionDioramaToon` (two-step soft toon ramp, rim, toon gloss, procedural caustics, a soft knee on reflected light so only emission blooms, an inverted-hull outline pass enabled only on creatures and characters, and the ShadowCaster, DepthOnly and DepthNormals passes URP's shadows and SSAO need), `EvolutionDioramaGlass` (fresnel glass and water, a small near-side glint, glow from the far side, a wobbling water top), `EvolutionDioramaUnlit` (flipbook particles) and `EvolutionDioramaWindow` (the street window, painted from a code-made mask). Volumes are made at runtime with only effects the project already uses (Bloom HQ, Neutral tonemapping, colour adjustments, white balance, vignette), so no shader variant is stripped. Materials are made at runtime from the classic ones and released with the world.
- **Lighting keys:** night, morning, midday and closing (`DioramaLighting`), blended over 1.6 s at a phase change and by the open day's progress (morning → midday → towards closing); sun colour, angle and intensity, ambient, the window sky, rooftops, lamp and stars, pendant lamps, a night tank glow, bloom and the shop and lab grades, which blend by where the camera is against the doorway. The room shell stops blocking the key light while the look is on, so the sun can tell the time.
- **The hatch hero moment** (`DioramaHatch`) keeps FX's cue durations (1.4 s first, 0.85 s repeat): wind-up with a dome squash and frame shiver, a 0.08 s presentation-only freeze beat with a ring flash (the game clock keeps running), the pop with a hand-drawn bubble cloud, puffs and sparkles, then the Pondlet turns to the camera, looks and blinks once. Repeat hatches have no freeze, flash or shiver; Reduced motion has none of them and a 6-bubble burst; Low halves the burst. It never blocks input; interruptions (pause, cards, focus loss, transfer during the wind-up) end it cleanly.
- **The kit** is generated by `Tools/Art/create_diorama_kit.py` in Blender 5.0 (original, local, no external assets): the Pondlet (front −Z) and the Casual visitor (front +Z) as rigid parts on the classic pivot names with face shape keys (Pondlet: Blink, Happy, Surprised, Puffed; visitor: Blink and four mouth moods), and the 512×768 flipbook (bubble, swirl, sparkle, puff, ripple, coin, four frames each). Unity reads the FBX exactly only with Unity coordinates reflected into Blender as (−x, −z, y) and every part directly under the asset root (import probes; nested parts came out moved and rotated), so each part is its own pivot and the visitor's face parts ride onto its head pivot at build time. Blender object names are global, so each asset is built and exported on its own. Provenance and hashes: `ArtSource/DioramaKit/manifest.json`.
- **Sizes:** the kit Pondlet is 0.9 of the classic model, then ×1.6 in display tanks and ×1.5 in the incubator, about twice its old on-screen size (AD.4); its swim amplitude is 0.82 in tanks so it stays inside the water.

**Found and fixed in this task's capture review:** the street window drew behind the painted trees; lit signs bloomed over their lettering (now the soft knee, with a check that reads the label off the screen in every key); the night water glow veiled the Pondlet (glow now from the far side); wide glass glints read as pale blobs inside the incubator; a creature facing the player from the incubator sat in its own shadow (a porthole fill light and a lighter creature shadow tone); the ring flash washed out the hatch; the customer reads its legs' vertices, so the kit is imported readable.

**Validation:** six numbered scratch players before one numbered final run (`Docs/Evidence/ad-a/Invoke-ADA.ps1 -Run 1`): **2,427 passed EditMode tests** (20 new in `DioramaSliceTests`), build 0 errors / 0 warnings, and **27,116 Windows checks** in 61 route steps: the AD-A route (`-evolutionDioramaSliceSmoke`, 948 checks) at 1280×720 and 1920×1080, the fresh-save cycle with the look on, and every route UX-09's final run passed, at 1280×720 with the look off. Measured cost on this PC (RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, i7-14700F, capped at 120 fps): up to about 0.3 ms CPU and 0.4 ms GPU at the incubator, nothing measurable at the corner. Evidence `Docs/Evidence/ad-a-VALIDATION.md`; source hashes `Docs/Evidence/ad-a/source-hashes.json` (56 files); review guide `Docs/Evidence/ad-a/PLAY.md`.

### AD.9 — AD-B implementation record (2026-10-22, Claude)

The user reviewed AD-A in game and approved it on 2026-10-22 ("check it good continue with the next AD"), which passed AD.7's gate; AD-B followed at once.

**Decisions (Claude, within AD.1–AD.7):**

- **Families on one rig:** the Brookkin (Pondlet, Bubblebelly, Ribbonfin), the Sparkline (Lanternfin) and the Airfin (Driftwing) share the pivot and face names the swim code already drives: Left and Right fin pivots, Tail pivot, Crest pivot (the Sparkline adds a Lantern pivot), and Body, Eyes, Pupils, Glints, Lids, Blush and Lips, with the shape keys Puffed, Blink, Happy and Surprised. Each species is its own flat kit asset (`DioramaBubblebelly`, `DioramaRibbonfin`, `DioramaLanternfin`, `DioramaDriftwing`, and the Pondlet rebuilt on the shared rig), built by `Tools/Art/create_diorama_kit.py` one asset at a time. `DioramaSpecies` (`Presentation/DioramaCreatures.cs`) lists each species' kit, family, atlas row, model, tank and incubator scales, swim amplitude, trick length and signature; AD-F adds rows.
- **Colour variants as one atlas:** `Resources/Art/DioramaKit/DioramaVariantAtlas.png`, 6 x 96 texels (Body, Fin, Belly, Accent, Blush, Sheen; a row for each species and variant, Classic, Sunny, Deep, Shimmer, counted from the top), imported readable, linear and point-filtered. Materials take their colours from it, and Shimmer turns on the toon shader's new iridescent sheen. Only the creature study shows variants for now; which specimen gets which colour is AD-F's (AD.3).
- **Tricks and habits are presentation only** (`DioramaTricks`): pure functions of the trick's age and the creature's clock, so they are EditMode-tested and never touch rules or saves. A trick plays when the player lingers 1.5 s at a display tank, then rests 8 s, as AD-A's Pondlet bubble does; it eases the creature to mid-water over 0.3 s and back after (`DioramaTricks.Settle`). Reduced motion plays none; Low effects detail halves their bursts.
- **Sizes** are each species' largest at which its trick stays inside the glass, measured by driving the real creature through the trick in EditMode (`EveryTrickStaysInsideTheTankGlass`): x1.6 Pondlet, x1.2 Bubblebelly, x1.25 Ribbonfin, x1.3 Lanternfin, x1.2 Driftwing in display tanks; x1.15 to x1.5 in the incubator.
- **Family water** (`DioramaWater`): a tint per family on each display tank's water through its property block, eased over a second when the resident changes; the water's far side carries it three times as strongly as its near side (the glass shader's new `_FarSide`), and the night key's glow takes the tint's colour, so it reads without veiling the creature. The incubator's fluid takes a hint of the family colour (its glow too), not more: the hatchery frame's back panel sits inside the fluid, so only its near side, in front of the creature, could carry a strong tint.
- **The creature study** (`StudyPresenter`, `ShopPresentation`, `ShopWorldSample`) shows Next species, Colour and Trick with the look on; the classic study is unchanged with it off.
- **Validation preview hook:** `PreviewResidentForValidation` shows any species in a display or the incubator without a saved specimen; it stays through the game's refreshes until the route clears it, and the tank's label reads PREVIEW meanwhile (development builds only).
- **UX-09's string guard** (`NoStringMentionsTheClassicUi`) now reads every string entry and skips only the colour-variant labels, since AD.3 names the first variant Classic; it still fails on any other string naming the classic UI.

**Found and fixed in this task's route and capture review:** the route's preview creatures vanished on the next model tick; the Driftwing's loop broke the glass by a centimetre while the static fit test passed (the loop turns the creature about its origin with its sails and tail swinging about theirs), so the test now drives the real creature; **the family water was invisible while every value check passed** (10–13% opacity, and the night glow, one cyan for every tank, drowned it), now the far side, the family glow and an on-screen check that was shown to fail on the old water; the tank close-ups showed tails behind the aim prompt; the incubator's family fluid could not be strong without veiling the creature.

**Validation:** thirteen numbered scratch players (number 11 a mutation player) before numbered run 2 (`Docs/Evidence/ad-b/Invoke-ADB.ps1 -Run 2`; run 1 stopped at its EditMode step on the string guard): **2,439 passed EditMode tests** (12 new in `DioramaCreatureTests`), build 0 errors / 0 warnings, and **37,913 Windows checks** in 63 route steps (60 in run 2; three rerun alone on the same player after losing window focus to a game being played): the AD-B route (`-evolutionDioramaCreaturesSmoke`, about 5,000 checks) and the AD-A route at 1280x720 and 1920x1080, the fresh-save cycle with the look on, and every route AD-A's final run passed, at 1280x720 with the look off. Measured on this PC with the Lanternfin performing: about 0.05 to 0.1 ms of main-thread CPU at 1280 x 720 with the look on; the look-on and look-off samples overlap at 1920 x 1080 and in GPU time; every frame at the 120 cap. Evidence `Docs/Evidence/ad-b-VALIDATION.md`; source hashes `Docs/Evidence/ad-b/source-hashes.json` (60 files); review guide `Docs/Evidence/ad-b/PLAY.md`.

### AD.10 — AD-C implementation record (2026-10-22, Claude)

The user looked at the creatures (AD-B) in game and approved them on 2026-10-22 ("check it good continue with the next AD"); AD-C followed at once.

**Decisions (Claude, within AD.1–AD.7):**

- **One humanoid rig, one builder:** every character is built by `humanoid` in `Tools/Art/create_diorama_kit.py` on the classic joint names (Left and Right hip, Body, Left and Right shoulder, Head pivot) and AD-A's face (Head, Eyes, Pupils, Glints, Lids with Blink, Blush, Mouth with Happy, Haggle, Shocked and Ouch, Left and Right brow pivots), so walking, work, comedy and reaction poses drive them all. Each role is its own flat kit asset: `DioramaCasualVisitor` (AD-A's, rebuilt and proved identical by geometry digest), `DioramaBargainVisitor`, `DioramaCollectorVisitor`, `DioramaPremiumVisitor`, `DioramaCrewCashier`, `DioramaCrewStocker`, `DioramaCrewTechnician`. AD.4's body types are per-role meshes from that builder, not shape keys: a shape key cannot move the rigid pivots the poses turn.
- **Who is who (AD.4):** Casual round (orange knit, beret, tote); Bargain hunter tall and thin (green knit, mustard scarf, flat cap, coin purse, elbow patches); Collector pear-shaped (plum coat, bow tie, grey hair and moustache, bowler, round gold spectacles, magnifier); Big spender a wide cream coat (dark lapels, gold buttons, carnation, top hat, gold gift bag). Crew always in shop teal (`DK_CrewTeal`), customers never: Pip (teal shirt, cream apron painted on, coral badge, visor, pencil) on a 0.3 m **step stool**; Nori (teal overalls, beanie, work gloves) with a wooden **carry crate**; Moss (long teal lab coat, mossy hair, goggles, a vial).
- **The role table** `DioramaRoles` (`Presentation/DioramaCharacters.cs`): each role's kit, crew or not, shoulder and head-top heights (the carry socket scales by the shoulder; the slap stars circle at the head top + 0.13 m), its squint and brow tilt while haggling or concentrating, and the four reactions per kind: customers Haggle, Happy, Shocked, Ouch; crew Focus, Happy, Shocked (caught out), Greet. The crew's face follows its work (`ResolveCrewMood`): a refused job, then a placed or checked-out job or a celebration, then greeting (Pip greets a customer, then concentrates once the sale is 45% rung up), then concentrating while working.
- **Rebuilding in place:** `ShopCharacterVisual.BuildForRole` builds the kit figure while the look is on, else the classic one; `RebuildForLook` swaps them in place when the look switches, keeping the owner's own children and the worker binding. The crew rebuild from `ShopSession.SetDioramaLook`; customers keep the look they arrived with until they leave. Pip's duty sign follows the figure's height (`ShopCashier.FitSignToActor`).
- **The character studies** (`StudyPresenter`, `ShopPresentation`, `ShopWorldSample`): with the look on, studies 4 and 5 show Next type / Next crew and Reaction; the title names the character and the reaction held; a look switch with a study open rebuilds its figure. With the look off they are the classic studies.
- **Validation-only hooks** (refused outside validation): `ShopCustomers.HoldVisitsForValidation` holds every visit's phase and timers so a reaction can be shown and read; `SendVisitorsAwayForValidation` ends every visit as a walk-out recorded in the day's ledger.

**Found and fixed in this task's route and capture review:** switching the look lost the rebuilt figure's joints (the old parts, destroyed only at the end of the frame, were found by name); after a switch Nori floated 0.26 m and Moss 0.20 m (the first idle pose used the old figure's resting hip height); Pip's duty sign covered the taller figure's visor; the visitors' close-ups were taken through the display glass; `ResetVisitors` leaves visits open in the day's ledger, which allows four; the kit's hands are part of its arms, so the hands-over-the-counter check reads the hand's own vertices.

**Validation:** eight numbered scratch players and two mutation players before numbered run 1 (`Docs/Evidence/ad-c/Invoke-ADC.ps1 -Run 1`): **2,447 passed EditMode tests** (8 new in `DioramaCharacterTests`), build 0 errors / 0 warnings, and **41,283 Windows checks** in 65 route steps: the AD-C route (`-evolutionDioramaCharactersSmoke`) and the AD-B and AD-A routes at 1280x720 and 1920x1080, the fresh-save cycle with the look on, and every route AD-B's final run passed, at 1280x720 with the look off. ### AD.11 — AD-D implementation record (2026-10-22, Claude)

The user looked at the characters (AD-C) in game and approved them on 2026-10-22 ("check it good continue with the next AD"); AD-D followed at once.

**Decisions (Claude, within AD.1–AD.7):**

- **The look everywhere by converting materials in place:** every classic lit material the world and the siphon show becomes the toon (or, if transparent, the look's glass) while the look is on, recorded (`DioramaConvertedMaterial`) and put back exactly when it is off; a material the game assigns later is already in the look. Surfaces spanning a room take the room style. Creatures, characters, text, particles, the FX pool, AD-A's corner swaps and the placement ghosts are left alone. The look's shaders carry a hidden `_Color` with the classic main colour, since game code reads `Material.color`.
- **Set pieces (AD.4),** one per wing, decorative children of the wing, in walls and ceiling (never on the arranged floor): shop wing 1 a bay window bench recessed into the front wall (the street through the window by the lighting key) and three hanging fish bowls; shop wing 2 a feature tank recessed into the front wall with caustic sand and a Bubblebelly, Ribbonfin and Lanternfin (kit creatures) on slow loops, glowing at night; lab wing 1 an overhead pipe gallery (four culture mains, rails, junction box, gauge, valve wheel); lab wing 2 a glass dome with Spark motes and Mist puffs once researched. A recess rebuilds the wall around its opening with the same panelling; the classic wall's collider stays. The classic wing art shows again with the look off.
- **Culture pipes (AD.4):** Bloom and Flow from their growers, Spark from the research bench, Mist from a working vat, each up to its own lane (3.30 to 3.60 m, 10 cm apart), across on a line of its own and down into the incubator's top beside the others; a glowing core by the grower's stock, three travelling beads, a pulse on every dose (by hand or module); rebuilt when a station moves.
- **The siphon (AD.4):** 0.46 against the classic 0.62, a slim side chamber (0.7 x 1.0 x 0.7 of the classic) still showing the carried cultures, at almost the classic place: 0.67 of the classic screen area.
- **Signs (AD.4):** the shop's, the lab's and each gallery's sign shows its name alone, 1.3 times larger, centred on its board; labels that tell the player something are untouched.
- **Flipbook moments (AD.5)** with the six shapes, replacing the pool's procedural accents while the look is on (the classic counters and cue ownership unchanged): the sale's scoop, bag tie and hop, with coins jumping from the counter (the money chip's own coins carry on); the slap's impact star, birds and spinning hat (every customer type's hat slots lifted out of the head mesh); a grey puff for every refusal or blocked action, the siphon also shaking; the price nod, crew work and comedy beats; fish bubble trails; caustic display and bowl sand; wobbling display water. Three sounds (bag tie, birds, puff) on the existing comedy voice while the look is on.
- **Comfort:** Reduced visual motion leaves only still puffs and glints (no hop, shake, coin jump, spin, birds, trails or travelling beads; the bowls still; a dose's pulse a gentle brightening); Low detail lets fewer particles go and one bead a pipe.

**Found and fixed in this task's route and capture review:** game code reading a converted material's colour logged errors (the toon had no `_Color`); the siphon still took 0.83, then 0.75, of the classic screen area (the classic one runs off the screen); the route's model-level dose raised no cue; the spinning hat outlived the slap's reaction and stayed hidden; the low-detail check counted the fish trails' particles; pipe lanes 8 cm apart would touch; the sale and slap views first stood behind display panels or the visitor's top hat.
